details.description: GPT-chat-latest is Microsoft Foundry's Azure-branded name for OpenAI's chat-latest alias, a continuously-updated pointer to OpenAI's current Instant-tier chat model (currently built on the GPT-5.4 and GPT-5.3-chat line). It replaced OpenAI's discrete gpt-5-chat and gpt-5.3-chat snapshots, which Azure's own retirement schedule lists as retired in favor of this rolling alias. It accepts text and image input and produces text output, with step-by-step reasoning available when useful, and is aimed at multi-turn assistants, tool-calling agentic systems and retrieval-grounded chat rather than deep, deliberate reasoning tasks. Azure lists it under a Preview lifecycle, and OpenAI's own docs for the alias recommend GPT-6 Astra instead of chat-latest for production API workloads.
advantages: OpenAI reports 52.5% fewer hallucinations and a 37.3% reduction in hallucinated claims on previously-flagged conversations, versus the prior GPT-5.3-chat snapshot, per Microsoft's Foundry launch announcement.
Produced roughly 25-30% fewer words than GPT-5.3-chat across common prompts while preserving response quality, per OpenAI's testing cited in the same announcement.
Supports step-by-step reasoning, function/tool calling, web and file search, and code interpreter tools through the Responses API (OpenAI's chat-latest model page).
disadvantages: OpenAI's own chat-latest documentation recommends using GPT-6 Astra instead of this alias for production API usage.
Is a continuously-updated alias: OpenAI states the underlying model snapshot will be regularly updated, so behavior can change without a version change.

Listed under a Preview lifecycle on Azure, not general availability; Azure's model retirement schedule shows the current August 2026 snapshot retiring December 2, 2026, matching the catalog's deprecation date.
use_cases: Multi-turn conversational assistants and customer-facing chat experiences
Tool-calling agentic workflows that orchestrate search, retrieval, ticketing or CRM systems
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) applications needing grounded, context-aware synthesis
Customer support, IT helpdesk, HR and sales-enablement assistants (Azure Foundry use cases)

sources.title: Introducing OpenAI's newest chat model in Microsoft Foundry | Microsoft Community Hub
Model retirement schedule - Microsoft Foundry | Microsoft Learn

notes: This Azure-only target (providers: azure) has no dedicated OpenAI docs page under the Azure product name 'gpt-chat-latest'; researched via OpenAI's own 'chat-latest' page (the underlying alias, confirmed to be the same model by Microsoft's launch blog: 'GPT-5.5 Instant (or Chat-latest in the API) ... as GPT-chat-latest'), Microsoft's launch blog, and Azure's model catalog/retirement schedule. OpenAI's chat-latest page gives a 400K-token context window and 128K max output tokens (400K-128K=272K input, matching the catalog's max_input_tokens exactly). Azure's own catalog quick-facts page separately states 'Context window 200k', which disagrees with the 272K figure derived from OpenAI's page; kept the catalog's 272000 value per instructions. Azure's retirement schedule independently confirms the current 2026-08-06 snapshot retires 2026-12-02, matching the catalog's deprecation_date exactly. The GPQA/AIME/MMMU-Pro/CharXiv-reasoning scores are OpenAI's own testing as relayed by Microsoft's blog (explicitly captioned 'Data shown comes from OpenAI's testing'); no independent leaderboard numbers for this specific alias were found.
